professionalSummary: Seasoned reconciliation analyst with two years of experience managing daily break‑handling for Visa and Mastercard settlements at a regional acquirer. Demonstrated ability to maintain and improve runbooks, onboard new analysts, and coordinate escalations with treasury and merchant services. Proven track record of documenting month‑end close notes and controlling the reconciliation workflow.
experienceHighlights: Executed daily break‑handling procedure, completing control checklist before 11:00 treasury cut‑off.
Rewrote reconciliation runbook post‑tool migration, adding screenshots and training two new analysts.
Escalated unresolved breaks above threshold to treasury and merchant services via formal escalation form.
Authored month‑end close notes detailing carried‑over breaks and analyst responsibilities.
Managed break handling, runbook maintenance, analyst onboarding, and escalation for the settlement reconciliation queue over ~2 years.
projectsAndWorkSamples: Revised runbook section on break classification with screenshots and verification trail.
Month‑end close note listing carried‑over breaks with ticket identifiers.
optimizedCv.evidenceBoundary: The provided resume and work samples confirm the candidate’s experience with daily break handling, runbook maintenance, escalation coordination, and month‑end documentation. They do not provide quantitative evidence of reducing average time to clear settlement breaks or explicit documentation of limitations and hand‑over conditions beyond the month‑end notes.

decisionBoundary.statement: Human review required to assess evidence gaps and interview‑signal risks.

evidence.text: Ran the daily break-handling procedure for Visa and Mastercard settlement files at a regional acquirer, working through the break queue in the reconciliation tool and ticking off the control checklist before the 11:00 treasury cut-off.
evidence.notes: Direct statement of daily procedure and checklist completion.

evidence.text: Rewrote the reconciliation runbook after the tool migration, adding screenshots for the new break-classification screen, and walked two newly hired analysts through it during their first fortnight.
Raised unresolved breaks above the agreed threshold to treasury and merchant services through the escalation form; the decision to hold or release a merchant payout stayed with the treasury manager.
Wrote the month-end close notes for the reconciliation queue, listing carried-over breaks, the reason each was open and the analyst taking it over.
evidence.notes: Shows documentation of limitations and hand-over conditions.

supportedClaims.claim: Candidate has run the daily break-handling procedure and maintained the control checklist.
supportedClaims.witness: Ran the daily break-handling procedure for Visa and Mastercard settlement files at a regional acquirer, working through the break queue in the reconciliation tool and ticking off the control checklist before the 11:00 treasury cut-off.

supportedClaims.claim: Candidate has rewritten the reconciliation runbook and trained new analysts.
supportedClaims.witness: Rewrote the reconciliation runbook after the tool migration, adding screenshots for the new break-classification screen, and walked two newly hired analysts through it during their first fortnight.

supportedClaims.claim: Candidate has coordinated escalations with treasury and merchant services.
supportedClaims.witness: Raised unresolved breaks above the agreed threshold to treasury and merchant services through the escalation form; the decision to hold or release a merchant payout stayed with the treasury manager.

supportedClaims.claim: Candidate has documented month-end close notes with carried-over breaks and analyst responsibilities.
supportedClaims.witness: Wrote the month-end close notes for the reconciliation queue, listing carried-over breaks, the reason each was open and the analyst taking it over.

unsupportedClaims.claim: Candidate has reduced the average time to clear settlement breaks to a measurable baseline.
unsupportedClaims.reason: No concrete data or baseline provided; only a vague claim of 40% faster without context.
unsupportedClaims.requiredFollowUp: Ask for specific metrics, baseline, period, and measurement methodology.

missingEvidenceGaps.gap: Quantitative evidence of average time-to-clear reduction, including baseline, period, and measurement method.

interviewSignalRisks.text: Candidate said that after the runbook rewrite breaks were 'cleared roughly 40 percent faster'; he thought the figure came from a team meeting slide but did not know the baseline or the period it covered.
interviewSignalRisks.recommendedHandling: Verify the claim with data from the candidate’s previous employer and request documentation of the measurement.

followUpQuestions.question: Can you provide the specific metrics, baseline, and period that demonstrate the reduction in average time to clear settlement breaks after the runbook rewrite?

humanReviewChecklist: Confirm that the candidate’s daily break-handling procedure aligns with the team’s published monthly baseline.
Verify the 40% faster claim with documented evidence.
Ensure that escalation coordination responsibilities match the job’s expectations.
Check that month‑end close notes include all required documentation of limitations and hand‑over conditions.
hiringEvidencePacket.auditSummary: The evidence confirms the candidate meets most role requirements, except for the quantitative reduction in settlement break clearance time. Human review should focus on validating this claim and ensuring all procedural responsibilities are fully documented.
limitations: Evidence is limited to the candidate’s resume and a recruiter note; no third‑party verification or performance data is provided.
